scope: Read-only, source-by-source comparison of the first20 occurrences in the owner-scope-or-detector-gap bucket of the current934-hold classification. This proposes routes; it changes no editorial decisions.
method: Read each complete inventory example, guide meaning and Book/question/sample/page locator; compare the exact proposed canonical meaning, grammar, target detector and existing target-bearing teaching examples.

For the broader-frame comparisons1524/1872/139/328/161, also inspect the existing listening/reply/scene/contrast/dialogue definitions to ensure the proposal does not redefine their specific original examples or keys.
Consult the listed primary dictionary/publisher evidence for uncertain constructions. Distinguish directly attested evidence from editorial application to this source.

Compile each proposed regex with the same JS i flag used by the runtime. Check full source recognition or the explicitly normalized teaching form, and preserve all current canonical strings recognized by the existing detector.
Patterns are deliberately bounded to the source forms reviewed here; they are not wildcard authorization of every possible object. Regex recognition alone does not prove the intended sense.

items.sourceSentence: Stop cutting it so fine and leave for the station earlier.
items.sourceGuideMeaning: Leaving almost no margin for error; a conventional expression about overly precise timing.
items.currentDecisionReason: Cutting it so fine expresses the same risky-timing idea as canonical 855, but the existing target pattern only detects cut it fine without so. Hold until the intensifier variant is reviewed and covered by its pattern and examples.
items.canonicalMeaningEn: Leave only a very small margin of time before a deadline or required arrival.
items.canonicalGrammar: be cutting it fine; cut it fine in present or past; this lesson focuses on time margins.
items.comparisonEvidence: The source is the same near-deadline, little-buffer sense. So intensifies fine; it does not change the idiom or prove arrival is already late.
items.requiredScopeAndGrammarChange: Add optional so before fine; explain degree while retaining the deadline/margin boundary.

items.sourceSentence: Please do not wait until the last minute to submit the form.

items.canonicalMeaningEn: Close to the relevant departure, event or deadline, leaving little advance notice; last-minute describes a late arrangement, while at the last minute locates an action or change.
items.canonicalGrammar: a last-minute trip uses a hyphenated adjective before a noun; change a plan at the last minute uses an adverbial phrase without the hyphen. The surrounding verb shows what was arranged or changed close to the relevant time.
items.comparisonEvidence: Waiting until the latest submission opportunity is the same last-minute timing family as the owner’s near-event arrangements. The difference is temporal construction, not a new lexical sense.
items.requiredScopeAndGrammarChange: Teach wait/leave something until the last minute as continuation or delay up to the latest opportunity. Keep at as the time of an action and last-minute as an adjective; broaden the title/meaning beyond trips without claiming the forms interchangeable.

cut.checkedSense: cut it/things fine: very little available time; cutting is the regular participle.
cut.limitation: The optional so degree word is a grammatical inference from the source, not a separately quoted dictionary headword.

last-minute.checkedSense: The entry groups at and until the last minute with the latest opportunity, alongside hyphenated adjectival last-minute.
last-minute.limitation: The prepositions mark different temporal relations; they are not freely interchangeable.

on-paper.checkedSense: Plan/theory-based appearance contrasted with practical operation; this is distinct from literal printing on paper.

eat-into.checkedSense: Using part of money or time is separate from damaging a material surface.

lean-into.checkedSense: Accepting a challenge and making effort.
